page: Amazon Web Services c8a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz with 1 thread per core. Memory allocation stands at 32.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is not bundled locally, meaning workloads rely on network-attached persistence, and default network bandwidth is rated at a baseline of 8 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated hardware accelerators are not included, yielding a GPU count of zero.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute efficiency, led by top-tier single-core and multi-core evaluations. The instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 2,807.0 and a multi-core score of 21,584.0, complemented by top-tier single-core stress-ng CPU output (3,776.99) and single-threaded gzip compression at 41.52 GB/sec. Instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 support dense mathematical operations, reflecting top-tier performance in image processing (21,778.0) and text processing (3,937.0). For lighter computational models, small-scale (135M) LLM text generation reaches a top-tier rate of 430.49 tokens/sec.

Resource-intensive workloads exhibit balanced mid-range characteristics. Multi-core stress-ng (59,718.9), PassMark CPU score (47,006.99), and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth (109.17 GB/sec) test within the average tier. Similarly, medium-scale (7B) model inference processes at 23.8 tokens/sec for generation and 124.05 tokens/sec for prompts. Software compilation via Clang (35,601.0) and database operations (20,831.18) deliver standard mid-range output.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, high single-thread throughput, and absence of local storage position the c8a.4xlarge as a cost-efficient deployment for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive in-memory footprints. Best-fit use cases include compute-intensive batch processing, high-throughput static web serving (measured at 52.84 GB/sec), distributed microservices, media encoding, and automated CI/CD pipeline workers.

The instance includes 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated local NVMe storage, and has no GPUs. The c8a.4xlarge fits compute-bound workloads including CI/CD build environments, batch processing, static web serving, and media transcode pipelines.
